newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Sept-Nov sugar output up 8.15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Sept-Nov sugar output up 8.15 pct.

text.p: Philippine raw sugar output during September to November, the first quarter of the 1996-97 crop year, increased by 8.15 percent to 313,020 tonnes from 289,419 tonnes in the year-ago perdiod, the state-run Sugar Regulatory Administration said.

Administration chief Wilson Gamboa said he expected the country's sugar production to reach between 1.9 million and 2.0 million tonnes in the current crop year from the previous year's 1.79 million tonnes.
"I expect production this year to equal demand," Gamboa said in an interview with Reuters.
The import of some 1.2 million tonnes of sugar from September 1995 to July 1996 had swamped the local market, he said.
Gamboa said the Philippines plans to export sugar at "competitive prices," to reduce stocks.
The plan will be finalised at a meeting on Thursday of a multi-sectoral committee with representatives from government and the private sector, he said.
The group was set up by President Fidel Ramos to solve problems arising from the current sugar glut in the market.
